name: Write Admission
definition: Accepts a write of an item from a writer inside the platform, and refuses a write that does not meet the contract.
rationale: Sources, agents and any caller that keeps the result of a live read write through one path (DEC-008). A contract that the receiver enforces cannot be gone around, and it covers a writer that nobody wrote a requirement for.

name: Item Custody
definition: Holds each item with the writer that the system stated, with the source that its writer supplied, with its times, and with the values that the item held before.
rationale: An item with no origin cannot be judged. A value with no history cannot be superseded, and a derivation cannot give the data that it used.

name: Identity and Supersession
definition: Matches an item that arrives against an item that it holds, makes one value current, and holds that an item no longer exists at its source.
rationale: REQ-PL-001 makes the platform give a current value, so the platform and not the reader decides which value is current. A removal has no later value and supersession does not cover it (DEC-017).

name: Provenance
definition: Tells an observed value from a derived one, gives the data and the time that a derivation used, and gives the writer, the source and the times of each value that it serves.
rationale: An inference that a reader cannot identify is given as a fact. A derived value decays when its inputs move on, and the reader judges it (DEC-011).

name: Exact Query
definition: Answers a query for the value of an item.
rationale: An agent needs an exact value.

name: Meaning Query
definition: Answers a query by meaning, and gives the items that relate to the subject of the query.
rationale: An agent needs the values that relate to a subject, from the same body of data. This is a different mechanism from an exact query, and one works while the other fails.

name: Admission by Position
definition: Refuses a read, a write and a removal that the position of the caller does not admit.
rationale: Agent Definition declares the position and what it admits. Each boundary refuses (DEC-019). This is the boundary for data.

name: Off-host Copy
definition: Makes the copy of life state away from the host, decides when to make it, and restores life state from it.
rationale: A consistent copy of a body of data is a property of holding that body. External Access carries the copy to the external service and does not decide (DEC-020).

name: Removal
definition: Removes one item, or everything that came from one source, when the user asks.
rationale: Life state is kept until the user removes it (DEC-021). Removal is the only thing that takes data out, and the user is the only one that starts it.

name: Kind Declaration
definition: Holds the kinds of item that life state accepts, and accepts the declaration of a new kind, a change to a kind and the removal of a kind.
rationale: A body of shapes that nobody declared cannot be enumerated, and makes a query by meaning worse with time (RSK-ST-001). The declaration is also the form that a writer converts into (DEC-025).

name: Subject Declaration
definition: Holds the declared subjects and their hierarchy, and accepts the declaration of a new subject, a change to a subject and the removal of a subject.
rationale: DEC-063. FUN-ST-10 holds the same capability for the kind of an item. MET-017 uses the functions as the coverage check, so a capability that no function states is invisible to that check.
